title: SDK transport auto-profile and latency-aware connection priming recipes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: ship cross-language SDK primitives and example recipes that automatically profile client workload characteristics and use those signals to tune connection pool size, keep-alive/idle timeouts, and connection priming behavior per-endpoint. Problem: customers see variable tail latency on cold routes (chat/streaming) and often choose conservative global connection settings that are either wasteful (too many spare connections) or fragile (insufficient priming for bursty workloads). This ticket scopes a lightweight runtime auto-profiler + set of adaptive defaults and cookbook examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that: 1) collect minimal metrics on request inter-arrival times (IAT), request durations, streaming session length, and observed TCP/TLS handshake times; 2) recommend pool resize and priming thresholds (e.g., pre-warm N connections when 95th IAT < X ms); 3) expose a small opt-in API (enable_autoprofile=true) and stable knobs to opt out or pin settings; 4) include runnable example recipes and testing harnesses for deterministic CI verification.
acceptance_criteria: Autoprofile feature implemented in Python/TS/Go SDKs behind opt-in flag: enable_autoprofile
SDKs emit standardized telemetry metrics (sdk.transport.autoprofile.*) documented in telemetry README
Default heuristic reduces median and p95 cold-start token latency for streaming routes in our lab harness by >= 20% versus baseline conservative defaults
Example recipes and README added to sdk-examples repo and CI integration tests added to ensure deterministic behavior in synthetic burst patterns
PRs merged with cross-language API parity (signature docs) and sample snippets in top-level SDK README
proposed_solution: Implement a three-part approach: (A) lightweight runtime profiler: tracks inter-arrival histogram, median/95th request durations, and handshake cost samples; stores exponentially-decayed statistics to avoid unbounded memory. (B) decision engine: small rule-set that maps profiled signals to pool size delta, priming count, and keepalive/idle adjustments. Rules are conservative by default and gated by a short 'warmup' window (30s of stable traffic). (C) recipes + telemetry: language-specific examples that wire autoprofile to existing transport stack, and emit metrics for verification. We will keep the runtime profiler as pure client-side logic (no telemetry upload unless user enables it), and export hooks so platform/instrumentation teams can opt to integrate signals into Console rollout or routing heuristics.

decisions: Autoprofile will be opt-in by default for 2026-03 release; opt-out for privacy and enterprise compliance
Profiled stats are client-only by default; telemetry emission requires explicit enable_telemetry flag
Initial heuristics use exp-decay windows and require >= 30s stable traffic before scaling pool up to avoid oscillation
Keepalive defaults will adapt only within safe ranges (+/- 50% of configured min/max) to avoid breaking firewalls or middleboxes
tradeoffs: Benefits: reduces token-level cold-starts for bursty streaming routes and provides actionable recipes for customers. Risks: client-side heuristics can mis-estimate in pathological workloads (e.g., very spiky traffic, long pauses), which is mitigated by conservative defaults, warmup windows, and explicit knobs. Additional complexity in SDK code paths increases maintenance surface; to mitigate, the profiler is implemented as a small dependency-free module with a stable public API and comprehensive unit tests.
